units.function: Database-backed regression tests for replaying every Company-scoped configuration row to a newly started singleton plugin worker, while filtering rows by plugin ID.
units.dependencyDirection: Company administrators persist plugin config through pluginRegistryService; one process is spawned per plugin across Companies; registry.listConfigs(pluginId) loads all tenant rows and the loader delivers their full configJson to that shared worker at startup.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID/key/package/version/apiVersion/manifest/capabilities/status/install order; Company; pluginConfig Company row; arbitrary configJson containing Slack bot/app token-shaped values.
units.lifecycle: Install a plugin; save separate Company configs; start one plugin-wide worker; list and replay every configured Company's values; return none if unconfigured and exclude other plugin IDs.
units.testAssessment: The three scenarios explicitly verify the intended startup replay and plugin-level filtering, but all were skipped locally because embedded Postgres was unavailable. The design test demonstrates a large multi-tenant secret blast radius: one worker receives complete config for every configured Company. It omits Company-authorized reads, isolation after worker compromise, config versions/order, acknowledgement, partial delivery and rollback, restart races, schema validation, secret reference resolution, redaction, rotation/revocation and upgrade compatibility. The assertions prove decrypted/raw token-shaped values reach listConfigs callers; they do not by themselves prove the database's at-rest encryption behavior.
units.designRationale: Allow proactive plugins to initialize Company-specific integrations before any Company-scoped invocation, compensating for a plugin-wide worker bootstrap that otherwise has no tenant config.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS extensions and Connectors must support proactive behavior without concentrating every enterprise tenant's secrets in a shared process or cloud control plane, especially for self-hosted/local execution.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT singleton-worker all-tenant full-config replay. Use declarative non-secret config revisions plus opaque SecretPort references. Bind each invocation or proactive subscription to one tenant/execution domain and capability set; resolve only required secrets just-in-time inside the customer's execution node; issue short-lived audience-scoped material; never return other tenant rows to the process. Require config schema/version, monotonic revision, signed delivery envelope, acknowledgement, health, rollback, rotation/revocation and audit events. Isolation may be per tenant, sandbox or connector node depending risk, but the security boundary cannot be plugin ID alone.
units.responsibilityConflict: A shared plugin process can act proactively for multiple Companies with all of their configuration, but no accountable human, purpose, responsibility contract, data scope or per-action approval accompanies startup replay. A compromised or confused plugin can therefore cross organizational responsibility and secret boundaries.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL multi-tenant blast radius: one plugin worker receives every configured Company's full config at startup. CRITICAL secret delivery risk: token-shaped Slack credentials are returned as raw config values rather than opaque references or short-lived scoped material. HIGH isolation gap: filtering by plugin ID prevents cross-plugin bleed but provides no isolation between Companies inside the same worker. HIGH lifecycle gap: no config revision/order, acknowledgement, retry, partial-failure, rollback, rotation or revocation behavior. HIGH authorization gap: listConfigs is not tested with a Company principal or per-tenant capability decision. MEDIUM compatibility gap: manifest apiVersion exists but startup config schema/version migration is absent. TEST GAP: all database-backed scenarios were skipped locally.
